name: PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk

frontmatter.title: J Resources Asia Pasifik — one mine, a large cash pile and a price that already assumes more
frontmatter.summary: PSAB sold its second mine and kept one: Bakan, a small Indonesian gold operation whose stated reserve supports only a few years at the current rate, plus a depleting Malaysian remnant and two non-producing deposits. The balance sheet is in net cash after the disposal. Our life-of-inventory DCF, with the other ounces valued in the bridge, puts fundamental value far below the market price; the twelve-month target keeps part of the premium. Initiate at REDUCE, target Rp377.
thesis: The Doup disposal reset the company from a two-mine, high-leverage producer to a single-mine, net-cash one, but the market still capitalises the smaller asset base at a large premium to our fundamental value.
Bakan's stated reserves support only a few years at the first-half run-rate; the conversion that would extend the mine is in the bull case, not the base, so the base carries no terminal value.
The interim dividend was funded by disposal proceeds, so the trailing yield is a capital return rather than a recurring payout; the forward dividend is a fraction of it.
At the current price the shares discount a gold price far above the one our sector deck carries, so the risk-reward is unattractive even after the target keeps most of the concentration premium.
The controlling shareholder holds almost all the shares and the public float is thin, which is why the platform applies its concentration lens to the twelve-month target.

catalysts.event: FY2026 annual report: Bakan reserve restatement, first full year without Doup, realised gold price
Free-float compliance step: the public float must reach the next tier, by controller sell-down or new shares
Index review after the free-float deadline: a compliant float could restore index eligibility
September-quarter filing becomes archivable; confirms post-dividend cash and debt
Any further step-up in the gold royalty schedule after the postponement announced in 2026

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of J Resources Asia Pasifik at REDUCE with a twelve-month target of Rp377 against a price of Rp436, a total return of -10.2% including the forward dividend of Rp14. The call rests on the shape of the company after the Doup sale: one producing mine, Bakan in North Sulawesi, a Malaysian operation that has been written down to a remnant, and a balance sheet that moved from heavy debt to net cash when the disposal proceeds landed [S2][S4]. Our primary method is a life-of-inventory DCF that carries no terminal value, because the ore body depletes and there is no second producing asset behind it; on the stated reserve alone it values the shares at Rp249 [S2][S3]. The ounces the company owns outside that reserve — Lanut, Seruyung and the Penjom probable block — are added in the bridge at sourced marks rather than left at zero, and the closure provision is deducted there [S2][S4].

The gap between that value and the market price is the whole argument. The price is 1.8 times fundamental value on our numbers, which is what a controlled, thinly floated Indonesian small cap often costs, and the platform's concentration lens therefore sets the twelve-month target at Rp377 rather than at our fundamental value [S2]. Even on that generous reading — a target that still keeps most of today's premium — the shares are worth less than they cost today. The two things that would change the call are a reserve conversion at Bakan that extends the mine beyond our forecast window, and a gold price that holds above the through-cycle mark in our sector deck; the two that would break it are a reserve downgrade and a large related-party use of the disposal cash [S2][S3].

We have deliberately not applied a default haircut to the base case. The forecast volume runs at the first-half run-rate only while the stated reserve lasts, the revenue line uses the deck's gold path and the company's own realised discount to it, and the cost base is the FY2025 unit cost escalated by the fuel path [S2][S4].

J Resources Asia Pasifik is an Indonesian gold producer listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Its producing asset after the Doup disposal is the Bakan mine, held through PT J Resources Bolaang Mongondow, which delivered the great majority of group output in FY2025; the balance came from Penjom in Malaysia, an operation that has been mined down to its last proven block [S2][S4]. Seruyung and North Lanut are in post-mining care and maintenance, so the revenue base is effectively one mine with one plant and one permitting envelope [S2].

The company reports in US dollars, sells doré and concentrate at internationally quoted gold prices, and charges the royalty in general and administrative expenses, not inside cost of sales [S2]. FY2025 gold production was 83.9 koz thousand ounces (F1), of which Bakan produced 77.4 koz thousand ounces (F14) and Penjom 6.5 koz thousand ounces (F15) [S2]. Net sales were US$289 USD mm (F5) against cost of sales of US$119 USD mm (F7), with a royalty charge of US$41.4 USD mm (F9) inside the operating cost line [S2].

The asset base is the whole investment case. Bakan carries compliant proven and probable ore reserves of 219 koz thousand ounces inside a measured, indicated and inferred resource inventory of 707 koz thousand ounces (F11, F12) [S2]. At the FY2025 mining rate the reserve block is only a few years of production, and our base case therefore mines the stated reserve and nothing else; the longer reserve sufficiency the company itself states depends on converting resource, which we carry in the bull case rather than the base [S2]. The group's other ounces are real but small: North Lanut holds 157 koz thousand ounces of proven and probable reserve inside a larger resource, Seruyung 184 koz thousand ounces of resource with no reserve, and Penjom 384 koz thousand ounces of proven and probable reserve, of which 379 koz thousand are probable (F31-F34) [S2]. We value Lanut and Seruyung at a sourced in-situ mark and Penjom at its post-impairment carrying value, all in the bridge, rather than at zero [S2][S4].

The group structure changed materially in the year. The Doup mine, held through PT Arafura Surya Alam, was sold to a subsidiary of the Astra group at an enterprise value of US$540 USD mm (F16), completing in February 2026, and the disposal produced a gain of US$298 USD mm in the first half (F17) [S3][S4]. Penjom was written down by US$103 USD mm (F18) and now carries US$16.5 USD mm (F21) after 4,734 oz ounces of its stated proven reserve had already been mined (F28) [S4]. The remaining group is a single-mine producer with a cash-rich balance sheet, which is a different company from the one that carried the debt we see in the FY2025 accounts [S2][S4].

The controlling shareholder is the President Commissioner, who holds 92.5% of the shares, leaving 7.5% in public hands, as disclosed in the capital-stock note to the FY2025 accounts [S2]. Management is therefore the same party as control, and the board's independence rests on the commissioner designated as independent [S2].

Gold is a price-taker's business: nobody in this industry sets the price, and the only durable advantages are ore grade, cost position, permitting and the ability to replace mined ounces with new reserves. Indonesian producers sell at the London price with a refining and treatment discount, so the realised price is the quoted price less a spread that moves with concentrate quality and refinery tightness [S2]. PSAB's own realised price in FY2025 was US$US$3,308/oz per ounce against US$US$2,310/oz per ounce the year before, which tracks the move in the quoted price rather than any company-specific premium (F3, F4) [S2].

The regulatory framework is the single most important non-price variable. Royalties on gold are set by government regulation and step up with the reference price: PP 19/2025 raised the rate to 16.0% once the gold reference price reaches the threshold in the schedule, replacing the earlier lower rate [S7]. The company's FY2025 royalty charge implies a blended take below the new rate because the higher schedule only applied for part of the year (F9, F5) [S2][S7]. A further increase was announced and then postponed in 2026, which is why we model the current schedule rather than a rising one [S6]. Permits are issued through the national mining regime, and the company's ability to keep Bakan's plan approved is a live operating risk rather than a theoretical one [S2].

The sector's cost structure is driven by diesel, labour, reagents and stripping. Fuel is the input we model explicitly, because the sector deck's Brent path and the company's own fuel intensity are both observable [S2]. Indonesian producers also carry a currency mismatch worth stating plainly: revenue is in dollars, a large part of the cost base and all of the dividend are in rupiah, so a weaker rupiah flatters margins and a stronger one compresses them [S2].

Competitive position is best described as sub-scale but cash-generative at the margin. Bakan's unit cost, on our own build from the LK, sits far enough below the deck's through-cycle gold price to keep the mine in cash through the cycle, which is what allows a small single-mine producer to earn a margin [S2]. We do not claim a quartile on a global all-in sustaining cost curve, because we cannot source a named third-party cost curve for Indonesian gold in the registry; the cost position is therefore our reconstruction rather than an industry ranking, and we treat the quartile as unverified [S2]. Against the larger Indonesian gold names the company has no diversification, no smelting or refining integration and a much shorter reserve life, and it competes for capital on yield and on resource conversion rather than on scale [S2]. That is a weak moat by any measure: the mine is valuable while the ore lasts and worth the rehabilitation liability afterwards [S2].

The demand side is macro rather than industrial. Investment demand responds to real interest rates, the dollar and official-sector buying, jewellery demand responds to the price in local currency, and industrial demand is a small share of the total, which is why a gold miner's shares move with the metal more than with its own operating news [S2]. Our sector deck carries a through-cycle path anchored on a lower real-rate environment than the one that prevailed when the metal last traded at these levels, and that mark is the number behind every revenue line in our model [S0]. The supply side responds slowly, because a new mine takes years to permit and build, so a price above the marginal cost of production persists long enough for existing producers to earn abnormal margins, which is the window PSAB is selling into [S2].

For an Indonesian operator there is a second cycle on top of the metal: the cost of diesel, the rupiah, and the fiscal terms. Each has moved against producers at different times in the past, and none of them is within the company's control. That is why the moat question is settled quickly here — the company has a cost position, not a franchise, and a cost position is only as durable as the ore body feeding it [S2].

Gold miners everywhere are price-takers, and the industry's history is a cycle of capital
destruction at the top of the price cycle and consolidation at the bottom. Indonesian gold
deposits are typically epithermal and porphyry-hosted, with grades that fall as mines deepen, so
reserve replacement is a continuous cost rather than a one-off discovery event. The country's
mining code has repeatedly changed royalty and divestment terms, which is why operators hold
permits and fiscal terms as first-order risks.

The FY2025 accounts are the last clean year of the old company. Revenue was US$288.8m, cost of sales US$118.6m, EBIT US$100.9m and EBITDA US$145.8m, with D&A of US$44.9m and capex of US$30.9m [S2]. EBIT is restated to the company's own operating profit of US$101 USD mm (F27), and D&A is restated to the notes: cost-of-sales depreciation and mining-property amortisation plus the G&A depreciation and amortisation make up the total, whereas the data pack carries only the non-cost-of-sales lines [S2]. With the full charge added back, EBITDA is the filing-consistent US$145.8m, not the pack's EBIT-plus-partial-D&A figure.

The first half of 2026 is not comparable to anything before it. Net sales rose to US$161 USD mm (F19) and attributable profit reached US$178 USD mm (F20), but that profit contains the US$298 USD mm disposal gain and the US$103 USD mm Penjom write-off (F17, F18), so the operating result is a small fraction of the reported number [S4]. Total equity was US$436 USD mm at the June balance sheet with unrestricted retained earnings of US$186 USD mm (F23, F24), which is the first time in the company's recent history that the retained-earnings account has been positive and unrestricted [S5].

Earnings quality deserves a flag rather than a footnote. The disposal gain is a one-off, the write-off is a one-off, and both sit in the same half-year, which means the reported profit line tells an investor almost nothing about recurring earning power [S4]. The other flag is the working capital line: the FY2025 closing balance sheet includes a large held-for-sale block, US$234 USD mm of assets (F29) and US$12.3 USD mm of directly associated liabilities (F30), which is why the pack's working capital jumps to US$224.3m in FY2025 and falls back afterwards [S2]. On a line-item build the operating balance was slightly negative at the FY2025 close — trade receivables, inventories and prepayments against trade payables, taxes payable and accruals, excluding cash, the held-for-sale block and all debt — so the company was funded by its suppliers rather than by its own working capital [S2]. We model operating working capital at a low single-digit share of revenue, consistent with the post-disposal balance sheet, and we do not extrapolate the negative balance because it rests on related-party and tax payables that need not recur [S2].

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the story and the easiest to state. At the June balance sheet the group held cash of US$17.1 USD mm and investments of US$195 USD mm against total liabilities of US$201 USD mm and equity of US$436 USD mm, so the disposal proceeds repaid the bank and bond facilities and left the group in net cash (F37-F39, F23) [S4][S2]. We take those lines from the primary H1-2026 filing as reported, and use the data pack only for the debt split and the non-controlling interest, which the archived filing does not break out; equity ties to the reported figure [S4][S0]. Against that, the company declared and paid an interim dividend of Rp793,800 IDR mm (F22), which is a cash outflow after the balance-sheet date and is treated as such in our bridge [S5]. Forward minorities are negligible because the non-controlling interest on the June balance sheet is a rounding item; we do not assert that the JRBM minority was bought in, because no price, counterparty or cash impact is sourced, and we flag the swing from the FY2025 minority as an open governance question rather than resolving it in our favour [S2][S4].

Our forecast runs the single mine to depletion. Volume starts at 78.5 thousand ounces in FY2026E, in line with the first-half run-rate, and is capped by the stated reserve, so the plan ends in FY2028 when that reserve is mined; the forecast window runs on beyond it with no production, which is why the terminal value is zero [S2]. Revenue follows volume times the deck's gold path and the company's realised discount, royalty is charged at the statutory rate, and cash cost is the FY2025 cost of sales less royalty, D&A and the inventory movement, escalated with the fuel path — a cash cost per ounce, not the accounting cost of sales [S2][S6]. EBITDA is US$176.0m in FY2026E and EBIT US$134.0m, with capex of US$28.9m and D&A of US$42.0m [S2]. Tax is charged at 33.0% of pre-tax profit, which is the cash rate the LK actually bears: the current-tax charges of the operating subsidiaries over the last two years average that level, and we carry it rather than the lower statutory rate because the non-deductible items in the current-tax line have not disappeared [S2]. The deferred-tax benefit that flattered the FY2025 effective rate is not extrapolated, and the statutory rate is used only for the debt tax shield in the cost of capital [S2].

The forecast table tells the story in one line: revenue and EBITDA fall after FY2026E not because the gold price falls but because the plan mines fewer ounces every year as the reserve block is consumed [S2]. That shape is the honest representation of a depleting asset, and it is why we carry no terminal value. Capex tracks the mine plan rather than growth, staying close to D&A, which is what a sustaining-capital business looks like once the growth project has gone [S2].

The cost build is deliberately simple and therefore checkable. We model the mined volume at the FY2025 stripping ratio, apply the FY2025 unit cost per bank cubic metre with the fuel share escalated on the sector deck's Brent path, and charge the royalty on revenue at the statutory rate; rentals and treatment charges sit in a separate cost line so that a change in the fiscal terms moves the model in one place rather than two [S2][S6]. The company's disclosure does not split diesel from the rest of the mining cost, so the fuel share is a sector-deck assumption rather than a company number, and we flag it as such [S0][S2]. The calibration test we care about is whether the model reproduces the FY2025 EBITDA at the FY2025 volume and price, and the residual is fully accounted for: part of it is the royalty step-up, which applied for only part of the year, and the rest is a sales-versus-production difference — revenue over the realised price implies more ounces sold than produced, an inventory drawdown the earlier note did not mention [S2][S7].

Capital allocation is the open question. The stated payout basis is a quarter of attributable profit, which is what the interim distribution was described as (F22), and we model that payout forward rather than extrapolating the disposal-funded distribution [S5]. The dividend capacity cross-check matters here: the forward payout is comfortably covered by forecast free cash flow once the one-off working-capital item is stripped out, but it is not covered by the trailing distribution if an investor assumes that distribution repeats [S2][S5]. Measured against our net asset value the forward dividend of Rp14 per share is a low-single-digit capacity yield, not the double-digit trailing figure the market quotes, which is the second reason the shares are not a yield substitute at this price [S5][S2].

A depleting single mine is valued on the cash it will produce before the ore runs out, so our primary method is a life-of-inventory DCF with no terminal value. Multiples are not value anchors for this name: the trailing earnings base contains loss years, a disposal gain and a write-off, and the peer set in Indonesian gold is priced on resource stories with very different reserve lives [S2][S4]. We therefore carry the DCF at full weight and disclose the multiple cross-checks as context only.

The discount rate is built from a dollar risk-free rate of 4.9%, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2%, an Indonesian country premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.08, giving a cost of equity of 12.1%; with a pre-tax cost of debt of 6.9% and a debt weight of 9.5%, the WACC is 11.5% [S0]. The debt weight is deliberately low because the group is in net cash after the disposal [S0].

The DCF produces an enterprise value of US$323.7m, and the equity bridge then adds the June investments and takes the net-debt position, subtracts the post-balance-sheet dividend, the working-capital correction described in section three and the closure provision, and adds the marks for the ounces outside the Bakan reserve [S0][S2][S4][S5]. The valuation date is 30 June 2026, the last balance sheet, and the horizon is twelve months from the price date, which is why the first forecast year carries only the part of FY2026 after the balance-sheet date. Both the dividend and the per-share value use the same spot rate of RpRp18,103/USD per dollar, so there is no cross-rate inconsistency in the bridge [S0].

Five bridge items are worth naming because they are large or contentious. The interim dividend of Rp793,800 IDR mm (F22) left the company after the balance-sheet date. The working-capital correction removes the discounted value of the FY2025 held-for-sale unwind: the net block is the US$234 USD mm of held-for-sale assets less the US$12.3 USD mm of directly associated liabilities (F29, F30), the model releases that balance in FY2026, and the bridge takes out the 30 June 2026 fraction of the release so the DCF cannot bank it twice [S2]. The closure provision of US$16.0 USD mm is deducted in the bridge rather than carried as debt, because it is a non-debt obligation and sits on the balance sheet as such (F36) [S2]. The debt definition used for the net-cash figure is total interest-bearing debt, which includes the related-party loan; that loan is therefore deducted once, inside net debt, and the related-party exposure is not double-counted in the bridge [S2]. And the three outside-reserve marks are added explicitly: Lanut at a per-ounce value between the Penjom impairment mark and the Doup transaction mark, Seruyung at a haircut to its resource for the absence of a reserve, and Penjom at its post-impairment carrying value (F31-F34, F21, F35) [S2][S4].

The reverse DCF is the cleanest way to state what the market believes. At the current price the shares discount a gold price of US$US$7,734/oz per ounce on our mine plan, against the US$US$4,300/oz per ounce through-cycle mark in our sector deck [S0]. At the spot price of US$US$4,075/oz per ounce the same plan is worth less than the deck case, and the benchmark rows of the sensitivity table bracket that value; we anchor on the through-cycle mark rather than on spot because the mine's revenue is priced off a path, not a point [S0]. That gap between the implied and the deck price is large, and it is the reason the rating is not a buy even though the balance sheet is strong and the dividend is real.

We do not add a separate special-distribution option on top of the disposal cash, and the reason is arithmetic rather than judgment: the cash and investments are already in the bridge at face value, so the value of the pile is captured once, and the deposit yield in the forecast is interest income on that balance rather than the value of the balance [S0][S5]. A distribution or a buyback at a discount to fundamental value would make the per-share value higher only by transferring value from sellers to holders, and no such programme is committed; we treat it as a signpost, not as base-case value [S2][S5].

Two readings of the sensitivity table matter. The first is the price elasticity: a change in the gold price moves the value more than any operating variable, which is the signature of a price-taker with a largely fixed cost base [S2]. The second is the discount-rate elasticity, which is larger than it would be for a long-life asset because the value is concentrated in the near years, so a higher rate shortens the effective life of the plan as well as discounting it [S2]. Neither reading argues for a wider method set: a multiple applied to these earnings would simply restate the same gold price with a different label [S2].

The concentration lens then sets the twelve-month number. The platform's konglo overlay applies to names the exchange lists for high shareholding concentration: PSAB is on the HSC list as of 22 October 2026, one shareholder holds 92.5% of the shares and the public holds 7.5%, and the registry requires the float to reach 12.5% by 31 March 2027 — a gap of 5.0% of the shares inside 4.7 months [S2]. That is a dated supply event, and it is why we do not assume the premium closes quickly. The step can only be met by the controller selling down or by new shares, and either route raises the tradeable base by roughly two-thirds while leaving control unchanged; a controller with a strategic stake has little reason to sell at a discount into a thin book, and new shares dilute the same controller. The base regime therefore closes 0.4 of the log gap in twelve months rather than all of it, the weighted target keeps most of the premium, and the index review by 30 June 2027 is the point at which a compliant float could bring index money in and compress the rest [S2]. We agree with the mechanism here and disagree with anyone who reads the target as a statement that the shares are worth that much today.

The largest risk is geological, not financial. The mine plan consumes the reserve block early and depends on converting resource into reserve at the historical rate; if conversion stalls, the operation runs off the stated reserve and the DCF ends years earlier than our base case [S2]. The bear case captures exactly that: gold below the deck's through-cycle mark, volume a tenth lower on reserve shortfall, realisation weaker and a higher discount rate for a single-asset producer, giving Rp202 [S2][S4]. The bull mirrors the discount-rate shock with a lower rate, so the scenario spread is not a one-sided conservatism [S2].

The second risk is the use of the disposal cash. A controlling shareholder with 92.5% of the shares can direct a large cash balance towards related-party transactions, and the group already carries loans from a related party on its balance sheet [S2]. The interim dividend is a shareholder-friendly use of the proceeds; a related-party acquisition would not be, and there is no commitment we can source that rules it out [S2][S5].

The third risk is regulatory and fiscal. The royalty schedule steps up with the gold price, so part of any price upside accrues to the state, and a further increase was postponed rather than cancelled [S6][S7]. Permitting, reclamation obligations and the post-mining liabilities at Seruyung and North Lanut are additional claims on cash that the operating forecast does not fully capture [S2].

The fourth is market structure. With 7.5% of the shares in public hands and a large controlling stake, the stock can move on flows rather than fundamentals, and the same concentration that supports the premium in the konglo lens makes the exit narrow if the premium compresses [S2]. The dated version of that risk is the float step: by 31 March 2027 the tradeable base must rise by 5.0% of the shares, and the mechanism is a controller sell-down or new shares [S2]. We do not add a fourth business scenario for it because the event changes the premium rather than the mine; instead the bear lens closes most of the gap, which is how the supply risk reaches the target [S2]. The average traded value is also small relative to the market capitalisation, which is why the platform applies a liquidity check before any position sizing [S0].

The bull case is not a heroic one. It assumes gold above the deck mark, Bakan converting measured and indicated resource into reserve at the historical rate — the only route by which the mine produces beyond our base window and into the next decade — a higher volume, and a lower discount rate, which together give Rp319 [S2]. The asymmetry between the tails is small on our numbers, which is itself the finding: the stock is a leveraged bet on a single ore body, and the balance sheet cushions the downside without creating much upside.

The signposts that would move us towards a more constructive view are a reserve statement that adds mineable years at Bakan, a decision to return the remaining disposal cash rather than redeploy it, and a gold price that holds above the deck's mark without a matching cost response [S2][S6]. The signposts that would move us the other way are a reserve downgrade, a related-party transaction that takes cash out of the operating company, or a distribution cut that signals strain [S2][S5]. We will also watch the realised discount to the quoted price, because a widening refining spread is the quiet way a gold miner loses margin while the headline price looks strong [S2].

Ownership is the defining governance fact. The President Commissioner holds 92.5% of the shares and the public holds 7.5%, a structure that puts the company on the exchange's concentrated-ownership list and out of the headline index calculation [S2]. Minority holders have no practical ability to block a related-party transaction, and the board's independent element is a single commissioner [S2].

The audit is clean on the face of the accounts, signed by a named partner at a recognised Indonesian firm, and the FY2025 statements carry the held-for-sale disclosures without a qualification [S2]. The related-party note shows loans from a related party and the usual service arrangements, which is normal for an Indonesian group of this size but is exactly where value leaks in a controlled company [S2]. The minority interest falls from a material FY2025 balance to a rounding item at June, and the materials we hold do not explain the change — no price, counterparty or cash payment is disclosed — so we treat it as an unresolved ownership question and credit no value to an assumed buy-in [S2][S4]. The reclamation and mine-closure provision is on the balance sheet, which is the right place for it, and we deduct it in the equity bridge rather than leave it as a footnote [S2].

The dividend record is short but real: a distribution paid in the middle of 2026 and the interim distribution paid after the June balance sheet, both described by the company as a share of attributable profit (F22) [S5]. The trailing yield looks extraordinary because it is measured against a year in which the company distributed disposal proceeds; the forward payout we model is a fraction of that, and investors should not capitalise the trailing figure [S5].

On ESG, the material exposures are mine-site water and tailings management, land rehabilitation after closure, and the social licence around artisanal mining near the Bakan tenement [S2]. The company discloses reclamation obligations but not a full emissions or water-intensity dataset in the materials we archived, so we treat environmental performance as unverified rather than as either good or bad [S2]. Governance is the binding constraint on the multiple in our view, not the environmental record.

The first catalyst is the FY2026 annual report, which will restate reserves at Bakan and give the first full year of accounts without Doup [S2]. The second is the September-quarter filing, which is already published on the company's investor site but has not been archivable in a form we can cite, so it is the first place we will look for the post-dividend cash position [S4]. The third is any further movement in the royalty schedule after the postponement announced in 2026 [S6]. The fourth is the free-float step: by 31 March 2027 the public float must reach 12.5% from 7.5%, and the way it is met — controller sell-down or new shares — is a dated supply event we will re-price as it approaches, with the index review by 30 June 2027 as the follow-on [S2].

Between updates we monitor four quantities: the quarterly production and realised price against our plan, the reserve and resource statement at Bakan, the cash balance and any related-party use of it, and the public float against the exchange's compliance calendar [S2][S5]. A reserve restatement that extends the mine beyond our forecast window would move the target before any change in the gold price does, and a related-party deployment of the disposal cash would move it the other way [S2].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: Gold mean-reverts below the deck's through-cycle mark, the Bakan reserve conversion stalls and the mine runs off the 219 koz reserve alone, so the plan ends around FY2029; Penjom closes after its proven block is exhausted and no new ore is found at Upper Tobayagan. Volume runs 10% below base, gold 20% lower, realisation a further 3% lower on a weaker refining market, and the discount rate 150bp higher for a single-asset, thin-float name.

bull.narrative: Gold holds above the deck's through-cycle mark and Bakan converts its measured and indicated resource into reserves as it has every year for twelve years, extending the mine beyond the five-year reserve-sufficiency window and restoring the FY2031-33 tail (about 120 koz) that the base case leaves out; Penjom's tailings retreatment stays economic at the higher price. Volume runs 10% above base, gold 20% higher, realisation 3% better and the discount rate 150bp lower for a name whose single-asset concentration is offset by a net-cash balance sheet in the up-cycle.

free float 7.48% must reach 12.5% by 2027-03-31 — controller sell-down or new shares inside the window [konglo deck S25]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Reserve-backed, not resource-backed, and capped at the stated reserve. Bakan has 219 koz proven and probable reserves (F12); no measured-and-indicated conversion is credited in the base because the company states only five years of reserve sufficiency at its 70-120 koz/yr capacity (S2 p.18), so the whole plan is 219 koz. FY2026E 78.5 koz is the sourced H1-2026 sales run-rate: H1 sales of US$160.63m (F19, S4) divided by the FY2026E deck price of US$4,288.84/oz and the 0.954 realisation gives 39.3 koz in the half, i.e. 78.5 koz annualised. FY2027E holds that rate and FY2028E 62.0 koz depletes the 219 koz reserve exactly; the engine then carries zero from FY2029E. There is no FY2031-33 tail in the base: the resource-conversion extension sits only in the bull narrative.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual, not on a forecast spike: the FY2025 average gold selling price was US$3,308/oz (F3, S2 p.45) against the metals deck's FY2025A gold average of US$3,466.09/oz, a ratio of 0.9544. The 4.6% discount is the refining and offtake wedge on Metalor sales (94% of 2025 revenue, S2 p.179) and is held flat across the forecast. It is NOT fitted to the FY2026E deck level of 4,493.75, which is a peak year relative to the FY2027E through-cycle marker of 4,300; fitting to the peak would carry a trough realised price into the long run.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic price cap applies to gold; all output is sold at market (S2 p.179).

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0: this is an ounces-based gold model, not a coal-style bcm stripping model, so cost_per_bcm carries the cash cost per ounce directly. PSAB does not disclose a strip ratio or ore tonnes in the annual report, and inventing one would be an unsourced driver.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Cash cost measured the house way (EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS): COGS less royalty less D&A. FY2025 COGS of US$118.568m (F7, S2 p.92) contains depreciation of US$22.527m and mining-property amortisation of US$17.225m (note 29, S2 p.179) plus an inventory movement of US$8.130m (stockpile, work-in-process and finished-goods lines, S2 p.179). The royalty of US$41.353m is charged in G&A (F9, note 30) and is modelled on its own line, so it is not in this input. Cash cost is therefore (118.568 - 39.752 - 8.130) = US$70.686m on 83.909 koz produced (F1) = US$842.4/oz. Held flat in nominal USD to FY2030E, per the house rule that costs stay at the last actual in real terms; no unsourced efficiency gain or further drift is assumed.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Diesel is the dominant mining consumable but PSAB does not split it out; the engine default of 0.3 is retained so the brent series can move the cost base without an unsourced split. The effect is immaterial because the oil deck is flat after FY2027E.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero by construction: the whole FY2025 cash cost per ounce (US$842.4, i.e. cost of sales less royalty, D&A and the inventory movement) sits in cost_per_bcm, and the royalty and SG&A are modelled on their own lines. Splitting the LK's single cash-cost line into mining and processing would be an invented allocation.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: PP 19/2025 sets 16% for primary gold when the HMA is at or above US$3,000/oz (F25, S7) and gold has been far above that since 2024; the May-2026 proposal for a further increase was postponed (S6). FY2025's effective take was 14.3% (royalty US$41.353m on sales US$288.751m, F9/F5) because the 10% rate under PP 26/2022 applied until April 2025 — a transition blend, not the forward rate. Using 16% is therefore a small step-up versus the last actual, disclosed in section 3.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Sales are gold and silver (S2 p.179); the silver credit is not separately disclosed and is inside the gold realisation, so carrying a separate line would double count it. Zero.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: No other revenue line is carried, so the margin is inert; kept at the engine default.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Total D&A from the LK notes, not the pack: COGS depreciation of US$22.527m plus COGS mining-property amortisation of US$17.225m (note 29, S2 p.179) plus G&A depreciation of US$4.816m and G&A amortisation of US$0.289m (note 30, S2 p.180) = US$44.858m (F42) on 83.909 koz produced = US$534.6/oz. The data pack's US$15.386m is only the non-COGS subset (the G&A lines plus the below-the-line mining amortisation), which is why it is restated from the filing. Held at the unit-of-production rate across the plan.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 additions were US$11.102m of property, plant and equipment, US$12.201m of mining properties and US$7.625m of exploration and evaluation (S2 p.94 cash flow) = US$30.927m on 83.909 koz = US$368.6/oz, which matches the pack's capex line. Held flat: the exploration share (US$91/oz) is genuinely discretionary, but after the Doup sale Bakan is the only asset and the company has kept drilling to replace reserves (132 holes in 2025, S2 p.53), so cutting it would be an unsourced uplift. No expansion capex is carried because no project remains.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero from FY2026E: the only development project, Doup, was sold to PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara and completed on 11 February 2026 for a US$540m enterprise value (F16, S3). Seruyung and North Lanut are in post-mining care and maintenance (S2 p.18/p.55), not development.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 pack figure (US$224.3m) is not operating working capital: current assets of US$332.007m include US$234.362m of Doup assets held for sale (F29) and current liabilities of US$182.191m include US$12.281m of liabilities directly associated with them (F30), so excluding the held-for-sale block operating working capital was about US$2.3m at 31 December 2025. After the disposal the 30 June 2026 balance sheet carries working capital of US$9.4m on about US$309m of LTM sales, i.e. 3.0% of revenue, which is carried flat. Prepaid taxes of US$21.9m (S2 p.90) are a period item and are not treated as operating. No stockpile release is modelled. The model still starts the FY2026E change in working capital from the contaminated FY2025 close, so the prorated difference is backed out in the valuation bridge.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The LK's cash tax rate, not the statutory rate. FY2025 current tax was US$23.997m on subsidiary pre-tax profit of US$70.085m (consolidated PBT US$65.364m less the parent's US$4.721m loss), a 34.2% rate; FY2024's current tax of US$15.205m on US$47.753m of subsidiary pre-tax profit was 31.8% (S2 p.92/p.187). The two-year average is 33.0%, which is used. The consolidated effective rate looked lower (19.0% in FY2025) only because of an US$11.598m deferred-tax benefit that is a timing item, not cash; the group's current-tax line has run well above the 22% statutory rate in both years because of non-deductible items and Malaysian tax at 24%. A forward 33% keeps that structural gap rather than assuming it disappears without a source.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest and finance charges of US$16.600m (S2 p.92) on opening debt of US$320.770m is 5.2%. Debt has since fallen to US$66.6m at 30 June 2026 after the Doup proceeds repaid the bank and bond facilities (S0 latest balance sheet), so the rate matters little; 5.2% is kept.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income was US$0.064m on US$28.3m of opening cash, about 0.2%. The post-sale cash balance is far larger (US$211.7m at 30 June 2026, S0), so 2.5% is used — a market rate on USD deposits, above the FY2025 actual but below a bond yield.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: debt fell from US$235.8m at FY2025 to US$66.6m at 30 June 2026 and the company has US$211.7m of cash (S0 latest balance sheet); there is no announced drawdown and the Doup proceeds are being returned rather than reinvested (F22, S5). Financing does not enter FCFF, so this only sets the interest path.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. The two large non-operating items of 2026 — the US$298m Doup disposal gain (F17) and the US$102.92m Penjom write-off (F18) — are one-offs already reflected in the June balance sheet and excluded from the forward operating model.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero forward. Non-controlling interests were US$115.2m at 31 December 2025, almost all of it the 20% of JRBM (Bakan) not owned (S2 p.179), but the 30 June 2026 balance sheet shows NCI of only US$0.01m (S0), so the minority has been bought in and the remaining subsidiaries are wholly owned. The FY2025 history therefore carries a much larger minority share than the forecast — the attributable earnings step-up is a real, balance-sheet-evidenced change, not an assumption.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The 2026 interim dividend of Rp793.8bn was explicitly set at 25% of the US$177.9m H1 attributable profit (F22, S5), and the June 2026 distribution of Rp105/share came out of the Doup proceeds. With the proceeds now largely distributed and the balance sheet net cash, 25% of earnings is the stated policy anchor and is carried forward. The dividend-capacity cross-check in section 4 uses this payout.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue or placement announced; the Doup proceeds funded the dividend instead (S5).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Inert: the primary method is a life-of-inventory DCF with no terminal value, because the mine depletes. Set to zero rather than the house inflation default so no residual growth can leak in.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 G&A was US$69.267m (S2 p.180), of which royalty was US$41.353m (F9) — royalty is modelled on its own line, so the SG&A ratio must exclude it: (69.267 - 41.353)/288.751 = 9.67%. Held flat. The FY2023-FY2025 pack default of 31.6% is meaningless because it includes the royalty and the loss years.

challenges.challenge: Omitted assets valued at zero: Lanut has 157 koz P&P (62 proved + 95 probable) inside 452 koz MII (S2 p.50/p.51) and Seruyung 184 koz MII, while Penjom 384 koz P&P includes 379 koz PROBABLE that the report discards by citing the 5,000 oz PROVED figure (F28, S2 p.50). The method says value everything owned and never zero a project; the stack can move HOLD to BUY.
challenges.answer: Base now mines only the stated 219 koz Bakan P&P; Lanut 157 koz P&P Seruyung 184 koz MII and Penjom 384 koz P&P (379 probable) are valued in the bridge at sourced marks (US$30.4m US$15.7m US$16.52m carrying value) and the closure provision is deducted; engine re-run.

challenges.challenge: Base volume of 478 koz over FY2026-FY2033 is 2.2x the 219 koz P&P and 96% of Bakan M&I (36 measured + 460 indicated = 496 koz), but the qc note claims it draws 478 koz at the historical 44% conversion ratio: 44% of M&I is 218 koz, not 478. The FY2031-FY2033 tail (120 koz) also runs past the company own five-year reserve sufficiency (S2 p.18) with no mine-plan source.
challenges.answer: Volume cut to the stated reserve: 75/75/69 koz over FY2026-FY2028 at the H1 run-rate then zero; the FY2031-FY2033 tail moved to the bull narrative; horizon five years with no terminal value; the 44% arithmetic in qc_justifications corrected and the drift.volume justification rewritten.

challenges.challenge: Tax is modelled at 22% while FY2025 current tax was US$23.997m, 36.7% of pre-tax (S2 p.92). The basis says statutory 22% plus the non-deductible items the current-tax line shows, which argues for a rate above 22%, not exactly 22%; the most-likely rule requires the LK effective rate unless a source shows the items disappearing.
challenges.answer: Forecast tax now 33.0% the two-year subsidiary current-tax average (34.2% and 31.8%) rather than the 22% statutory rate; the deferred-tax benefit is not extrapolated and the statutory rate is used only for the debt shield; the value effect flows through the re-run.

challenges.challenge: The HSC lens is supported by fund record (every HSC-listed name) and cov_konglo show (konglo true; HSC 2026-10-22; free float 7.48%; next step 12.5% by 2027-03-31), and the arithmetic ties (v 284.08, premium 1.535, base c 0.40 gives 394.8, weighted 1.3109 gives 400.3). But section 4 gives no name-specific reason why the base closes 40% of the gap for THIS name, as the card requires: no float math, deadlines, flows, group support or supply analysis, and the controller must lift float 5.02pp (about a 67% increase in tradeable supply) within 4.7 months.
challenges.answer: Lens kept and made name-specific: HSC listing 22 October 2026 float 7.48% versus a 12.5% floor by 31 March 2027 (5.02pp gap in 4.7 months) plus the index review by 30 June 2027; section 4 now explains that the step can only be met by a controller sell-down or new shares which raises tradeable supply by roughly two-thirds while leaving control unchanged so the base closes only 40% of the log gap.

challenges.challenge: The US$145.1m net cash (about 36% of equity value) and US$0.01m June NCI are sourced only to Yahoo Finance (S0); the 30 June 2026 primary statements are not used and the 30 September filing is unarchived. Yahoo is a secondary aggregator and a US$50m error moves value about 18%.
challenges.answer: June 2026 cash 17.06 investments 195.35 liabilities 201.35 and equity 435.50 now come from the primary H1 filing (F37-F39 F23) and tie to the reported equity; the debt split and the 0.01m minority are the only pack inputs and the source hierarchy is stated in section 3.

challenges.challenge: FY2025 NCI was US$115.2m and June 2026 NCI is US$0.01m; the report asserts the JRBM minority was bought in but gives no source for the price, counterparty or cash impact. If it was a related-party buy-in funded from Doup proceeds it is precisely the value-leak channel the report worries about, and it is unexplained.
challenges.answer: The unsourced buy-in assertion is removed: the report now states that no price counterparty or cash payment is disclosed so the June minority is taken as reported the swing from FY2025 is flagged as an unresolved governance question and no value is credited to an assumed buy-in.

challenges.challenge: The equity bridge deducts neither the US$16.0m reclamation and mine-closure provision (S2 p.91) nor confirms the US$38.2m related-party loan is inside the US$66.6m June debt. The report says the provision is on the balance sheet, which is the right place for it, but does not take it out of equity value.
challenges.answer: The reclamation and mine-closure reserve of US$15.97m (F36) is now deducted in the equity bridge as a non-debt obligation and the debt definition is stated: total interest-bearing debt including the related-party loan deducted once inside net debt.

challenges.challenge: The US$145m net cash is about 23% of market cap; the base pays only 25% of earnings and assumes the rest earns 2.5%. A special dividend, buyback at a discount to fundamental, or reserve-conversion capex funded from the disposal proceeds is not valued, though the report itself lists returning the remaining disposal cash as a signpost.
challenges.answer: The report now states that the cash and investments enter the bridge at face value so the deposit yield is interest income on the balance rather than the valuation of it; no special-distribution option is added because no programme is committed and the balance is already counted once.

challenges.challenge: The bear adds 150bp to WACC while the bull gets no matching -150bp (qc scenario.mirror says bear only val.wacc); the justification is a structural judgment, not a source, so the fundamental value is biased down and the target inherits it.
challenges.answer: The bull now carries the mirrored -150bp WACC shock (target op add value -0.015) so both tails are symmetric; the scenario.mirror justification records the mirror and the report says the spread is not one-sided conservatism.

challenges.challenge: The 2027-03-31 free-float step from 7.48% to 12.5% is a dated 5.02pp sell-down or placement inside 4.7 months, about a 67% increase in tradeable supply. Only the lens handles it; the business scenarios have no dated supply shock and section 4 does not analyse whether the controller can or will sell into a thin market.
challenges.answer: The float step is now a dated supply event in the catalysts and in sections 5 and 7: 5.02pp of shares by 31 March 2027 inside 4.7 months met by a controller sell-down or new shares with the index review by 30 June 2027; the bear lens closes most of the gap so the supply channel reaches the target without a fourth business scenario.

challenges.challenge: The held-for-sale bridge text says US$234.4m of Doup assets net of US$12.3m of liabilities gives US$214.9m; it gives US$222.1m. The US$108.3m value does tie to delta_nwc 214.68m x the FY2026 fraction 0.5038, so the model amount is right and only the derivation is wrong.
challenges.answer: Bridge narrative corrected: the held-for-sale net block is 234.4m less 12.3m (F29-F30) and the 108.3m item is the 50.4% FY2026 fraction of the 214.7m working-capital release from the 30 June 2026 valuation date.

challenges.challenge: The 3% nwc ratio rests on about US$2.3m at December 2025, which is not reproducible from the cited current assets 332.007m and current liabilities 182.191m (those give -72.3m before stripping current debt). The June US$9.4m figure is sourced only to S0.
challenges.answer: Line-item build stated: trade receivables plus inventories and prepayments against trade payables taxes payable and accruals excluding cash the held-for-sale block and all debt leaves operating working capital slightly negative at the FY2025 close so the company was supplier-funded; the 3% ratio is a normalisation for payables that need not recur and the June balance is not in an archived filing.

challenges.challenge: The report claims Bakan cost sits in the lower half of the Indonesian gold cost curve with no source and no quartile, and it does not state NAV at spot gold or a dividend-capacity yield versus the NAV anchor, all required by the VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL output contract.
challenges.answer: The unsourced quartile claim is removed: no named third-party AISC curve for Indonesian gold exists in the registry so the cost position is stated as our own reconstruction and the quartile as unverified; NAV at spot (deck gold spot versus the through-cycle mark with the sensitivity rows bracketing it) and the forward dividend-capacity yield versus NAV are now in sections 3 and 4.

challenges.challenge: The DCF FY2026 fraction of 0.5038 implies a 30 June 2026 valuation date while the price date is 27 October 2026, so the twelve-month target is about eight months forward; the interim dividend is also converted at 18,350 (deck FY2027) while the equity value uses 18,103 (spot), a US$0.6m inconsistency.
challenges.answer: Valuation date 30 June 2026 and the twelve-month horizon from the price date are now stated and the first-year fraction is explained; the interim dividend and the per-share value both use the same spot rate of Rp18,103 per dollar so the former 18,350 cross-rate is gone.

challenges.challenge: The -12.8% FY2025 calibration gap is justified only by the 16% royalty step-up (about US$4.7m); the rest is the production-versus-sales volume difference: revenue 288.75m divided by ASP 3,308 gives about 87.3 koz sold versus 83.909 koz produced, an inventory drawdown the note does not mention.
challenges.answer: Calibration reconciled in full: the residual is the royalty step-up that applied for part of FY2025 plus a sales-versus-production difference where revenue over the realised price implies more ounces sold than produced an inventory drawdown now named in section 3.

missing_bull_case.note: Lanut (157 koz P&P, 452 koz MII) and Seruyung (184 koz MII) are held at zero, Penjom 379 koz probable is discarded, and the US$145m net cash is assumed to earn 2.5% rather than be returned; all are upside absent from the base.

missing_bear_case.note: FY2025 current tax was 36.7% of pre-tax (S2 p.92) against 22% modelled; the US$16.0m closure provision and US$38.2m related-party loan are not clearly in the equity bridge; the 5.02pp free-float step by 2027-03-31 is a dated supply event not in the business scenarios.

assumption_realism.note: Volume of 478 koz over eight years is 2.2x the 219 koz P&P and 96% of Bakan M&I (496 koz), versus the 44% conversion the qc note cites (218 koz) and the company own five-year reserve sufficiency; tax at 22% sits below the LK cash rate; the 3% nwc claim is not reproducible from the cited totals.

evidence_and_citations.note: The load-bearing US$145.1m net cash and US$0.01m NCI come only from Yahoo (S0), not the 30 June 2026 primary statements; the held-for-sale bridge text says 234.4 minus 12.3 equals 214.9 (it is 222.1); the cost-curve claim is uncited.

valuation_method_fit.note: Life-of-inventory DCF is the right primary method and the HSC lens is supported by fund record and the registry (konglo true, HSC 2026-10-22), and its arithmetic ties; but the equity bridge omits the closure provision, the valuation date/horizon is ambiguous, and the output contract cost-curve quartile and NAV-at-spot are missing.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is measured and the DCF/lens split is transparent, but the one-mine framing and zero resource marks lean bearish while the HOLD target rests entirely on the lens; doubling the bear probability still leaves HOLD, so the rating is not one heroic input.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Gold, realisation and royalty read the decks consistently (FY2027E 4300, 0.9544, 16%); however the through-cycle mark is a deck forecast point rather than a named 10y series or incentive price, and the required AISC quartile is not stated.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack of understatements: zero Lanut/Seruyung, Penjom probable excluded, 3% positive nwc, capex held flat nominal while relying on 96% M&I conversion, no special distribution from net cash, and a bear-only +150bp WACC. The omitted reserves alone can move HOLD toward BUY.

calibration.note: The -12.8% FY2025 calibration gap is attributed only to the 16% royalty step-up (~4.7m); the remainder is the production-versus-sales volume difference (revenue 288.75m / ASP 3,308 = ~87.3 koz sold vs 83.909 koz produced) and is unreconciled.

signoff.notes: Batch bias check: the REDUCE is name-specific, not a shared input. The gold deck FY2027E 4,300 sits above spot 4,075, so the price path flatters the name; the 16% royalty is the PP 19/2025 schedule and the filing itself shows the effective take rising to 14.3% in FY2025 as the rate stepped up; the 11.5% WACC sits mid-band. What produces the call is the konglo lens reading, which I accept: fundamental 12-month value 263 against a price at 1.76x, with the target keeping 1.436 of that premium rather than assuming convergence, plus an HSC float step from 7.48% to 12.5% by 31 March 2027. The template-cannot-see-the-business risk was the right thing to test: the DCF runs only the 219 koz Bakan reserve and every excluded asset is valued, not zeroed - Lanut 30.4m, Seruyung 15.7m, Penjom at the company own recoverable-amount mark of 16.52m after the H1-2026 impairment - so the residual conservatism sits in the sourced mark, disclosed in section 4 and the bridge. C1 FATAL is fixed (omitted assets now bridged), tax moved to 33% on the filing, bear WACC shock mirrored. Approved.

bias.note: The round-1 cost error is genuinely gone: I re-derived cash cost of US$842.4/oz from note 29 (COGS 118.568 less depreciation 22.527 and mining-property amortisation 17.226 less the 8.130 residual) over 83.909 koz, and D&A of US$44.858m from note 29 (22.527 + 17.226) plus note 30 (4.816 + 0.289). EBITDA 100.915 + 44.858 = 145.773m matches the filing and the model. The forecast uses the same 842.4 base with the disclosed fuel escalation (about 946/oz in FY2026E), so there is no double count. Volume 78.5 koz ties to H1 sales 160.63m / (4,288.84 x 0.954) = 39.3 koz in the half and is capped at the 219 koz Bakan reserve, which is the sourced hard number. Bear and bull now carry mirrored WACC shocks (C9). Residual optimism in the Lanut/Seruyung marks is about Rp1.2/share and is argued between the Penjom and Doup marks. No directional bias either way. [S2][S4]

findings.finding: Section 3 and the cost_per_bcm basis say cash cost is cost of sales less ROYALTY, D&A and the inventory movement, but the arithmetic (118.568 - 39.752 - 8.130 = 70.686) does not subtract royalty, and the same report correctly states that royalty sits in G&A, not in COGS. A reader who recomputes the stated formula gets about US$350/oz, not 842.4. Section 3 also still describes the build as using the FY2025 stripping ratio and a unit cost per bank cubic metre with rentals and treatment charges in a separate line, whereas strip_ratio is a 1.0 placeholder, the cost is per ounce and other_cost_unit is zero.

Section 5 still says the base mine plan depends on converting resource into reserve at the historical rate and that the DCF ends years earlier if conversion stalls, although the base now mines only the stated 219 koz reserve and credits no conversion; the sentence is left over from the withdrawn 478 koz plan. The judge raises the same point.
Fact F42 carries the right total of US$44.858m but its quoted evidence shows only the note 10 depreciation of 22.527m, not the amortisation and G&A components that make up the sum.

flags.message: a.volume moves -100% from FY2026E to FY2030E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The base is the stated reserve and nothing else: Bakan has 219 koz proven and probable (F12) and the model draws exactly 78.5 + 78.5 + 62.0 = 219 koz over FY2026E-FY2028E, then zero. FY2026E 78.5 koz is the sourced H1-2026 sales run-rate: H1 sales of US$160.63m (F19, S4) divided by the FY2026E deck gold of US$4,288.84/oz and the 0.954 realisation gives 39.3 koz in the half, i.e. 78.5 koz annualised, not the old 37.5 koz arithmetic. The step down to 62.0 koz in FY2028E is reserve depletion, not a demand forecast; no resource conversion is credited in the base and the old FY2031-33 tail sits in the bull narrative only. [S2][S4]

flags.message: ebit FY2024A restated at 1.86x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's FY2024 EBIT of US$32.934m is restated to the company's operating profit of US$61.199m from the financial highlights (S2 p.5): the pack deducts charges that the LK reports below the operating line. The same restatement for FY2025 to US$100.915m is within the 50% threshold and is disclosed in section 3. [S2][F41]

flags.message: balance-sheet cash restated at 0.08x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack's June cash of US$211.7m is a single cash line; the H1-2026 filing splits it into cash of US$17.06m and investments of US$195.35m, including restricted time deposits (S4). Restating both lines keeps total liquidity at US$212.4m, so the equity value is unchanged in substance while the composition is now sourced to the primary statements. [S4]

The report states this explicitly. [S2][S4]

The 12-month target therefore keeps part of the premium the market pays over the life-of-inventory DCF instead of converging to it in one step; the fundamental value is disclosed separately in section 4 and the ownership consequence is discussed in section 6.
